items.title: Dorothy Tait Interview, 1968-12-21
items.q: The little waitress came up to me. Her name, it turned out later, was Sayuri Yamamoto... Sayuri Yamamoto noticed how interested I was... she told me... he was coming to Japan

ctx.x: Okay, so then, now tell us about the—you went to Japan. You were into France. You were in Japan at the same time the store was there, weren't you?

I was in Japan visiting a cousin who lives in Tokyo in 63. This was the summer, I think August 63. And, uh, was wandering around Shibuya, which is the area in which he lived. And each—this is a small section of Tokyo, and it has its own small bar district and red light district, whatever. And it's up a hill behind some buildings and it's alleyways. And I was walking alone, feeling very western and very out of place. When suddenly this same sound that I'd heard in 1945 comes banging out onto the street. And it's a…
